propositions: Plan-review Pass-1 lacks a criterion to detect when a ticket's own acceptance criteria and Scope/Out-of-Scope declarations are mutually unsatisfiable, leaving contradictions undetected until late stages and forcing costly re-reviews.

A new 1-TURN criterion `ac-satisfiability` in the `coherence` facet must own detection of three shapes of set-quantification conflicts: universal-vs-carve-out, derived-artifact closure, and snapshot cardinality.
The G3 child-coverage criterion is silenced by its roster carrying only child ids and titles, preventing it from testing whether siblings' acceptance criteria cover each parent criterion.

The sibling roster expression is duplicated across three independent callers (pass1.py, fidelity_spot_eval.py, eval_solver.py), creating maintenance risk and divergence in the eval harnesses that would corrupt dogfooding data.

The roster must be extracted as a shared `build_sibling_roster` helper, enriched with child acceptance-criteria items, and moved from per-pairing instructions into the system prompt prefix to avoid quadratic token re-sending.
The roster's token cost must be included in the `parent_tokens` prefix estimate to prevent bin-packing and cache-gating decisions from exceeding window budgets.
